papers.summary: We introduce NEOPIC, a framework for learning the field operator in particle-based methods applied to kinetic plasma simulations. Its key novelty is a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid, and is evaluated at the particle positions. No mesh or tree is needed and, unlike grid-based neural operators, no deposition onto a mesh takes place, so the particle noise that dominates the inputs of particle simulations is not aliased. Since it replaces only the field solve, it serves as a plug-and-play field solver for particle-based methods: it can be trained on data from particle-in-cell, particle-in-Fourier or tree codes, and combined with any time integrator, including implicit schemes. We prove that the discrete evaluation coincides with the continuous operator at any number of particles (representation equivalence) and derive an error analysis that separates sampling, learning and time-stepping errors: up to the learning error, NEOPIC has the error structure of standard Monte Carlo particle methods. We show that the particle noise in the training data acts as an implicit regularizer, which gives guidance on the number of training particles in relation to the particle numbers used at inference. A complexity analysis shows that NEOPIC is an $O(N_p)$ method whose constants are set by the architecture alone, independently of any mesh or tree. Numerical experiments on electrostatic benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron mini-app and a Penning trap, confirm the theoretical findings. A single model trained on several mini-apps generated by different reference methods captures all of them and remains stable up to twice the training time window, which points towards foundation models for fields in particle-based methods.
papers.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations

papers.summary: We prove quantitative sub-ballisticity for the self-avoiding walk on the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d\geq 2$. Namely, we obtain an explicit exponential rate of decay for the probability that a self-avoiding walk of length $n$ reaches distance at least $vn$, in terms of $v>0$. As a consequence, we show that the displacement of an $n$-step self-avoiding walk is at most $n/\exp(c\log^* n)$ with very high probability. Previously, only a non-quantitative $o(n)$ bound was known from the work of Duminil-Copin and Hammond. Along the way, we show that at criticality the partition function of bridges of length $n$ is on average bounded by $C/\log\log n$, which we believe to be of independent interest. Our approach is based on a quantitative analysis of the original nonconstructive proof of Duminil-Copin and Hammond using ideas from proof theory.
papers.title: Quantitative sub-ballisticity of self-avoiding walk on $\mathbb{Z}^d$

papers.summary: Recently, Krukowski characterised the classical Fourier transform on the real line in terms of its behaviour with respect to differentiation. For locally compact abelian groups, he obtained a characterisation based on the behaviour of the Fourier transform under the shift. Each of these results assumed that the operator (to be characterised) is an integral transform (with a kernel satisfying suitable regularity conditions), paired with a normalisation which he refers to as the Dirac delta property. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Here, the differentiation property is formulated in terms of the behaviour of the group Fourier transform with respect to the left-invariant vector fields, and the shift property is based on its behaviour under right translation. Both of these characterise the group Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, once paired with a Dirac delta property. Our results assume that the transform is continuous and linear, and do not require it to be an integral transform a priori.
papers.title: Differentiation and Shift Property Characterisations of the Group Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group

papers.summary: This paper presents a Lagrangian framework to solve Wasserstein Hamiltonian flows (WHF) under two-point boundary conditions on large finite graphs. Characterized by a coupled system of discrete master equation and Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) equation on the probability simplex, this formulation defines the macroscopic WHF. While classical density-based solvers can track this flow, they face severe memory and computational bottlenecks as the graph scale grows. To bypass these limitations, we introduce the stochastic Hamiltonian process (SHP), a sample-based mathematical framework that tracks individual particle dynamics rather than the full node-wise density. We parameterize the time-dependent potential using neural network, yielding the Neural SHP solver. Numerical experiments on synthetic graphs demonstrate the scalability of our method relative to density-based baselines. Furthermore, we validate Neural SHP across two large-scale real-world networks, a PubMed citation network and a massive road network, demonstrating its robust efficiency for graph partition and routing problems on complex graph structures.
papers.title: A Parameterized Stochastic Hamiltonian Process on Graphs with Two-Point Boundary Conditions

papers.summary: For every nonconstant real polynomial P of degree k and every positive rational exponent a/b, minimizing the spherical energy with potential |P(t)|^{a/b} admits a discrete solution with at most $\binom{d+2ak-1}{2ak}+\binom{d+2ak-2}{2ak-1}$ support points, where a/b is reduced. This finite-replacement consequence needs no denominator threshold. Under a multiplicity-sensitive denominator condition, we prove the stronger conclusion that every minimizer has an explicit uniform support bound; suitable negative positive-semidefinite perturbations preserve that bound. We present these consequences before the machinery. The main arguments simplify irrational-power finite-rank rigidity and give a Nash-curve ramification obstruction, stable under entire scalar additions, for powers, logarithms, and rational poles. The latter yields uniform finite supports on compact semialgebraic curves without assuming that the supports are semialgebraic. The known p-frame finite-replacement principle is distinguished from the extensions developed here. No unconditional discreteness theorem for general irrational p is claimed.
papers.title: Finite-rank rigidity and Nash-curve discreteness for correlation potentials

papers.summary: Motivated by Zygmund's differentiation conjecture and Stein's conjecture for Lipschitz vector fields, we study bilinear singular integral and maximal operators along variable curves given by $$ \begin{aligned} BH_a^α(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g\left(x + a(x)t^α\right)\,\frac{dt}{t},\\ BM_a^α(f,g)(x) &= \sup_{r>0}\frac{1}{2r}\int_{-r}^{r} \left|f(x-t)g\left(x+a(x)t^α\right)\right|\,dt,\\ BSH_c^α(f,g)(x) &= \operatorname{p.v.} \int_{\mathbb R} f(x-t) g(x + t^α)\, \frac{dt}{t-c(x)}, \end{aligned} $$ where $α> 0$ and $a,c:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ are measurable. For every $α>0$ and $0<A<B<\infty$, we construct a smooth, globally Lipschitz coefficient $a:\mathbb R\to(A,B)$ such that, for every Hölder conjugate pair $1<p,q<\infty$, no strong--type $L^p(\mathbb R)\times L^q(\mathbb R)\to L^1(\mathbb R)$ estimate holds for $BH_a^α$ or $BM_a^α$ on $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\times C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$; moreover, there exist nonnegative smooth inputs in $\bigcap_{s>1}L^s(\mathbb R)$, one of which is compactly supported, whose outputs under $BH_a^α$ and $BM_a^α$ do not belong to $L^1(\mathbb R)$. For any measurable $a:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $BM_a^α$ maps $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R)$ boundedly into $L^r(\mathbb R)$ whenever $1<p,q\leq\infty$, $1/r = 1/p + 1/q$, and $r > 1$, and maps $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R)$ into weak $L^1(\mathbb R)$ when $1/p+1/q=1$, with constants independent of $a$. Finally, we investigate the shifted operator $BSH_c^α$, including dyadic-integer-valued $c$, and prove that there is a measurable choice of $c$ such that the operator admits no bounded $L^p(\mathbb R) \times L^q(\mathbb R) \to L^{r,\infty}(\mathbb R)$ estimates in the range $1 \leq p,q \leq \infty$ and $\frac{1}{2}<r<\infty$, resolving an open problem posed by Gaitan and Lie.
papers.title: Bilinear operators along variable curves

papers.summary: This paper presents a numerical investigation of soft-to-hard terminal constraint convergence for optimal control problems governed by a second-order ordinary differential equation and the one-dimensional heat equation. The study complements the analytical convergence theory through comparisons with exact solutions and independently computed numerical approximations. For the heat equation, a fully discrete Crank--Nicolson finite-difference formulation is validated against exact modal solutions, exhibiting approximately second-order convergence in the terminal-state and midpoint-sampled control errors under simultaneous space-time mesh refinement. Numerical experiments demonstrate the predicted first-order penalty convergence for benchmark problems and investigate the admissibility threshold governing finite-energy exact terminal controllability. Additional modal experiments examine the dependence of terminal-error convergence rates on spectral regularity, illustrating intermediate rates consistent with the theoretical estimates and asymptotic predictions. The results provide computational evidence supporting the soft-to-hard convergence framework and clarify the roles of discretization, target admissibility, and spectral regularity.
papers.title: Numerical Investigation of Soft-to-Hard Convergence: Discretization, Admissibility, and Spectral Regularity

papers.summary: The singular value decomposition (SVD) provides optimal low-rank approximations of real and complex matrices by the Eckart--Young theorem, and SVD-based tensor decomposition algorithms such as the higher-order singular value decomposition (HOSVD) and the tensor train singular value decomposition (TT-SVD) inherit quasi-optimality guarantees from it. We extend the SVD to matrices over a finite-dimensional $\ast$-algebra $K$. Our main contribution is a characterization of the algebras $K$ for which every matrix admits an SVD, and of the inner products on $K$ for which the Eckart-Young theorem holds. We introduce a notion of ordered SVD, show that ordered SVDs reveal the rank of a matrix over $K$ and yield optimal truncations, and give an explicit algorithm that computes an ordered SVD from the structure of the algebra. We then extend the Tucker, tensor train, and tree tensor network (TTN) decompositions and their SVD-based decomposition algorithms to tensors over $K$, and show that TT-SVD retains a quasi-optimality guarantee over every such $K$, whereas HOSVD, ST-HOSVD, and TTN-SVD do so when $K$ is commutative. Viewed in real or complex coordinates, these constructions give novel decomposition formats of ordinary tensors. We illustrate our new methods by compressing data from a variety of scientific applications, and show that they can achieve lower approximation error than their classical counterparts at equal storage.
papers.title: Singular value decompositions over $\ast$-algebras with applications to tensor decompositions

papers.summary: Given a collection of mathematical objects and a natural notion of equivalence (such as isomorphism), we want to find a complete classification. This paper presents methods for proving anti-classification results, that is, when a complete classification is not possible using certain classifying invariants. The problem of using real numbers as classifying invariants is well understood. In this case, the obstruction to classifiability is ergodicity. We consider classifiability by higher rank objects, such as countable sets of real numbers, and present a simple ergodicity-like obstruction for classifiability. This method is particularly useful when applied in various models of ZF where even weak fragments of the axiom of choice fail.
papers.title: Ergodicity as an obstruction to classification by higher-rank invariants

papers.summary: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of the abstract endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by Keel and Tao. Our method is based on the near-far decomposition technique, which was developed in a recent work by Toyoshima and the author.
papers.title: An alternative proof of the Keel--Tao endpoint Strichartz estimates

papers.summary: We prove that every set $S = \bigcup_{n \geq 0} [ t_{2 n + 1} , t_{2 n} )$, where $t_0 > t_1 > \cdots > 0$ and $t_n \to 0$, admits no Riesz spectrum. This extends the result of Kozma, Nitzan, and Olevskii \cite{KNO} to a wide class of countable unions of intervals.
papers.title: Countable unions of intervals without Riesz spectra

papers.summary: Neural networks are commonly used to learn the solution operators of PDEs such as the Navier-Stokes equations and viscous conservation laws. On standard benchmarks, moderately sized and often shallow networks achieve small errors that decay at algebraic rates with the network size. These observations are not well described by the current approximation theory, which treats the solution operator as a generic map and derives worst-case bounds over large classes of operators. We show that the structure of the equations and their properties explain the observed behavior. For semilinear parabolic equations, the approximation costs separate into two terms, where one is controlled by an invariant of the governing law and the other by the data. The constitutive law can be parameterized as a single block whose size for accuracy $η$ is $O(η^{-pχ}\logη^{-1})$ for every $p>p_f$, where the structural exponent $p_f$ only depends on the computation graph of $f$. This exponent does not depend on the dimension and is in fact zero for polynomial laws, so for the two-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations the nonlinear block costs only $O(\logη^{-1})$ parameters. The data enters through encoding layers with a bounded number of learned weights per mode, so neither term grows with the grid resolution or the time step. While the analysis only uses the max-norm error of the pointwise block, we show that one obtains approximation bounds in a stronger norm along the whole trajectory. For viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations with a $C^s$ Hamiltonian, the approximation requires on the order of $η^{-1/s}$ parameters, and we prove a matching lower bound, up to logarithms. This shows that solution operators for this class of problems have low structural complexity, even though they are nonlinear maps between infinite-dimensional spaces.
papers.title: Neural Network Approximation and Structural Complexity of Semilinear PDEs with Lower Bounds

papers.summary: We study local derivations and local automorphisms of finite-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie and right Leibniz algebras. We prove that every non-abelian Lie algebra in this class admits both a local derivation which is not a derivation and a local automorphism which is not an automorphism. The constructions use a derivation $D$ satisfying $0\ne D([L,L])\subseteq Z(L)$. For non-abelian right Leibniz algebras, both existence statements hold whenever the dimension is at most seven or the nilpotency class is at most four. We construct an eight-dimensional non-Lie algebra of class five satisfying $\LocDer(A)=\Der(A)$ and $\LocAut(A)=\Aut(A)$. Consequently, eight and five are the least possible dimension and nilpotency class, respectively, for either equality.
papers.title: Local Derivations and Local Automorphisms of Arbitrary Finite-Dimensional Nilpotent Lie and Leibniz Algebras

papers.summary: We study the density of ergodic subrelations in the canonical Polish space of subequivalence relations of a probability-measure-preserving countable Borel equivalence relation. Our main result establishes rich ergodicity for ergodic treeable equivalence relations. The proof combines a strongly increasing exhaustion with relative ergodic hyperfinite decomposition. As an application, for every $2\leq r<\infty$, we show that the product of the dyadic odometer action of $\mathbb{Z}$ with the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{F}_r$ has a richly ergodic orbit relation, whereas the Bernoulli action of $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{F}_r$ does not. Thus rich ergodicity of a free ergodic action is not determined by the acting group.
papers.title: Ergodic treeable equivalence relations are richly ergodic

papers.summary: Differential calculi on non-irreducible quantised flag manifolds of the $\mathrm{A}$-series have recently been investigated using Lusztig positive root vectors, revealing that several features of classical differential geometry persist in the noncommutative setting. We extend this investigation to quantised flag manifolds associated with the lowest-rank quantum groups of types $\mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ whose classical spaces are holomorphic contact manifolds. Building on the Heckenberger--Kolb framework, we construct covariant first order differential calculi. The maximal prolongations of calculi restricted to contact directions have lower dimensions than their classical counterparts. In type $\mathrm{C}_2$, however, adjoining the Reeb direction yields a three-dimensional calculus on the contact flag manifold whose maximal prolongation has classical dimension. Adjoining the remaining simple-root direction yields a four-dimensional calculus on the full flag manifold, again with a maximal prolongation of classical dimension. For both calculi, we explicitly present the exterior algebras and identify them with those of the corresponding framing calculi on the quantum group. In type $\mathrm{D}_4$, we show that adjoining the Reeb direction yields a nine-dimensional calculus on the contact flag. We conjecture that its maximal prolongation also has classical dimension.
papers.title: A Dolbeault complex for the contact quantised flag manifolds of type $\mathrm{C}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{D}_{4}$

papers.summary: A \emph{Johnson graph} $J(n,k)$ is a graph whose vertices are the $k$-element subsets of an underlying set of size $n$ where two vertices are adjacent if they intersect in a subset of size $k-1$. We extend the definition to allow infinite parameters and we study a natural limit theory $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ of Johnson graphs. We show that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is complete and we give an axiomatisation of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, from which we obtain a complete description of the models of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$. We use this to show tameness properties of $T_{\mathcal{J}}$, namely that $T_{\mathcal{J}}$ is $ω$-stable of Morley rank $ω$, but not monadically dependent. In particular it follows that the class of all finite Johnson graphs is stable, and therefore dependent but not monadically dependent.
papers.title: Model Theory of Johnson Graphs

papers.summary: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.
papers.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture

papers.summary: Let $K$ be a field and $L_K(E,w)$ the Leavitt path algebra of a row-finite weighted graph $(E,w)$. Suppose that $L_K(E,w)$ is not isomorphic to an ordinary Leavitt path algebra. We prove that the ideal lattice of every countably generated unital $K$-algebra embeds as a closed interval into the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$. The embedding preserves multiplication of ideals modulo the lower endpoint of the interval. It follows that the ideal lattice of $L_K(E,w)$ is not distributive and that ideal multiplication in $L_K(E,w)$ is not commutative. Moreover, we show that if $(E,w)$ is countable, then $L_K(E,w)$ has exactly $|K|^{\aleph_0}$ ideals, prime ideals, left primitive ideals, and right primitive ideals.
papers.title: A note on the ideal lattice of a weighted Leavitt path algebra

papers.summary: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schröer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.
papers.title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules

papers.summary: For a strictly increasing $G:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ with $G(0)\geq 1$, we study minimal-basis function algebras generated by recursion along generalized inverses of its iterates. Bounded recursion requires an earlier pointwise majorant; unbounded recursion has no such requirement. If the orbit $G^{[t]}(0)$ has no polynomial upper bound, we obtain exact fixed-function membership spectra, reverse-divisibility inclusion, and indexed intersections that need not be single-stride algebras. Every finite divisibility-downset is realized in both regimes, and mixed strides admit fixed functions expressing any finite monotone Boolean condition on their additive stride monoid. For every generator, the realized bounded spectra form a bounded meet-semilattice: a construction sharing a bounding input coordinate realizes finite intersections without an unrestricted selector. Polynomial orbit growth is equivalent to definability of each of ordinary predecessor, unary doubling, and addition in any fixed unbounded stride algebra. In this case the algebra is ordinary primitive recursion relative to its inverse map, giving full collapse for primitive-recursive $G$. Ordinary predecessor belongs to a bounded stride algebra exactly when the orbit is polynomially bounded and $G$ has bounded successive differences; equivalently, ordinary bounded recursion embeds. A locality obstruction explains the additional bounded requirement, and two primitive-recursive generators with quadratic orbits have opposite bounded collapse behavior.
papers.title: Step Recursion: Exact Membership Spectra, Mixed Strides, and Collapse
